clue.text: Herald is offensive grabbing bottom in front of the queen

indicators.note: in front of places the first piece ahead of the second in the answer
one piece grabbing another holds it within its own letters

parts.note: the Tet offensive was the 1968 campaign in Vietnam, so offensive gives TET
rump means bottom, the backside
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: A rude herald gets hold of someone's backside before the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' looks like an adjective for rude, but it is the Tet offensive of the Vietnam War.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumpeter is a herald who announces arrivals with a fanfare.

clue.text: Doubles of whiskey, getting figuratively canned

indicators.note: the whiskey is getting put inside, held within the outer letters

parts.note: something canned is put in tins, so the cans themselves are TINS
Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Double measures of whiskey, with the drinker ending up metaphorically drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canned' looks like slang for drunk, but read literally it means put into tins: W goes inside TINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Twins are doubles, two people who look exactly alike.

clue.text: Initially under cross-examination one's admitted being related to the wife

indicators.note: Initially takes just the opening letter of the word under

parts.note: a cross is drawn as X

indicators.note: one admitted to a place goes inside it, here inside the examination

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's is only a link

explanation.surface: Under cross-examination, a witness admits being married to the defendant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross-examination' reads as one legal term but splits: cross gives X, examination ORAL, with I admitted into ORAL to make ORIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Uxorial comes from Latin uxor, a spouse, and describes things belonging to a married woman.

clue.text: Father gets married in ceremony

indicators.note: father gets the letter inside him, enclosing it

parts.note: pop is an informal word for a father

explanation.surface: Dad marries in a formal ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomp is stately display and splendour, the trappings of a grand occasion.

clue.text: Join up in a little ring

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to knit is to join, as bones knit together

explanation.surface: Get together within a small circle of friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little ring' suggests a small circle, but it is a light ringing sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A tink is a short, light chiming noise, like a small bell being struck.

clue.text: Settle again with theology lessons: in school, English …

parts.note: RE, religious education, is the school subject that teaches theology
the punctuation mark printed in the clue is itself a colon, and its name supplies the letters
I is an abbreviation for in, used mostly in barred puzzles

explanation.surface: Settling again, with scripture classes at school in English, leads on to the teachers in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon looks like mere punctuation, but it is part of the wordplay: its name gives five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To recolonise is to establish settlers in a territory once more.

clue.text: Horror film about a necromancer's origin

indicators.note: about means going round, so the film word surrounds the rest

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a film

indicators.note: origin takes the first letter of necromancer

explanation.surface: A scary film about a sorcerer's beginnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horror film' looks like one phrase, but Horror alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden overwhelming fear, terror.

clue.text: … teachers use God pages, endlessly adapted

indicators.note: adapted means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged
endlessly drops the final letter of the word pages

explanation.surface: Teachers make use of pages from scripture, trimmed and revised for the lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' strips the last S from pages, leaving PAGE; USE GOD PAGE is then reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedagogue is a schoolmaster or instructor, often a strict or pedantic one.

clue.text: Brief French refusal by telegram is uninterrupted

parts.note: non is the short French word for no
telegrams used the word stop in place of a full stop

explanation.surface: A curt French no sent by telegram is delivered without pause.
explanation.walkthrough: In old telegrams STOP was spelt out to mark the end of a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-stop means continuing without a break or pause.

clue.text: Careful on board! Extremely! One's a dangerous sucker at sea

parts.note: chary means wary or careful

indicators.note: Extremely takes the first and last letters of board

parts.note: one is I, and the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A warning shouted on deck to take great care of a perilous hazard at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' sounds nautical, but board simply gives its first and last letters, B and D. CHARYBDIS was the whirlpool of Greek myth opposite the monster Scylla.
explanation.definitionFit: Charybdis is the mythical whirlpool in the Strait of Messina that swallowed ships, drawing them under.

clue.text: Press guy is a superhero

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
a guy is a man

explanation.surface: A newspaper fellow turns out to be a caped crusader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' suggests journalism, but it means smoothing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron Man is the armoured Marvel comics hero Tony Stark.

clue.text: Solo passage from port between Cuba and South Africa

indicators.note: between puts the port in the middle, flanked by the two country codes

parts.note: C is the international vehicle code for Cuba
ZA is the international code for South Africa
Aden is a port in Yemen

explanation.surface: A lone voyage from a harbour between two distant countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadenza is a virtuoso solo section in a concerto, played without the orchestra.

clue.text: Drunkenly drink a schooner perhaps

indicators.note: a drunk's slurred speech turns the s sound into sh, so the word comes out changed

parts.note: to sip is to drink in small mouthfuls

explanation.surface: A sozzled sailor downs a large glass of sherry.
explanation.walkthrough: A schooner is also a tall sherry or beer glass, which fits the drinking surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a sailing vessel with two or more masts, so it is one example of a seagoing craft.

clue.text: A bit of land acquired by cunning

indicators.note: acquired by means taken in and held by the other word

parts.note: sly means cunning
to light is to land or settle, as a bird lights on a branch

explanation.surface: A plot of land obtained through trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'land' looks like a noun for ground, but it is the verb, to come down.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly means to a small degree, a little.

clue.text: The ten commandments?

parts.note: God's commandments are sacred instructions, read here as sacred instructions in the sense of ordination into the ministry

explanation.definitionFit: Holy orders is the status of ordained clergy, and orders can also mean commands that are holy.

clue.text: New shed you designed as location for play

indicators.note: designed means planned out, so the letters are laid out in a fresh pattern

explanation.surface: A garden shed newly built for children to play in.
explanation.walkthrough: A Wendy house is a British name for a child's playhouse, named after Wendy in Peter Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wendy house is a small toy house that children go inside to play.

clue.text: Good evening you and I note before the first of November?

definitions.text: Good evening you and I note before the first of November?

parts.note: hallo is a greeting, the sort said on meeting someone in the evening
you and I together are we
E is a musical note

indicators.note: the first of takes the opening letter of November

explanation.surface: A greeting shared by two people on the night before November begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the occasion: an evening that comes just before 1 November.
explanation.definitionFit: Halloween is 31 October, the eve of All Saints' Day on 1 November.

clue.text: Hydrogen increased about one mil had corporal twitching

parts.note: H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen
one is the Roman numeral I
a mil is a millilitre, and one millilitre is one cubic centimetre, CC
upped means increased

explanation.surface: A soldier's hydrogen dose was raised slightly, leaving him jerking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporal' looks like an army rank, but here it means bodily. 'about' reads as approximately before 'one mil' and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To hiccup is to have a sudden involuntary spasm of the diaphragm, a bodily jerk.

clue.text: Yawned in the middle of having a pedicure

indicators.note: in the middle of says the letters sit inside the run of words having a pedicure

explanation.surface: Someone yawned while getting their feet done.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaped means opened the mouth wide, as one does in a yawn.

clue.text: Stooge found in modern address within city limits

indicators.note: within puts the web address inside the city's outer letters
the limits of the word city are its first and last letters

parts.note: a URL is a web address, a modern kind of address

explanation.surface: A fall guy tracked down via a web address inside the city boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: Curly was one of the Three Stooges, the American slapstick comedy trio.
explanation.definitionFit: Curly Howard was a member of the Three Stooges comedy act.

clue.text: Deserts fighting among communists

indicators.note: among places one word inside the other

parts.note: reds is a common name for communists
war is fighting

explanation.surface: Soldiers desert while fighting breaks out among communist troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deserts' looks like a verb or arid land, but it means just deserts, what one deserves.
explanation.definitionFit: Deserts here is the noun from deserve: what someone has earned, good or bad.

clue.text: 9IT desk set -organised storage for IT!

indicators.note: organised means put into order, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A computer desk kit sorted with somewhere to keep the data.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of IT DESK SET gives the old floppy disks used to store computer files.
explanation.definitionFit: Diskettes are floppy disks, removable media once used to save computer data.

clue.text: Plays instrument casually. Having only gums, gets disheartened endlessly

indicators.note: disheartened removes the heart, the central letter, of that word
endlessly removes the final letter of the toothless word

parts.note: someone with only gums has no teeth, so is toothless

explanation.surface: An old musician with no teeth left plays half-heartedly and gets ever more fed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' takes out the middle H of TOOTHLESS and 'endlessly' its last S.
explanation.definitionFit: To tootle is to play a wind instrument idly or in a casual way.

clue.text: Peacekeepers quarrel over your old base

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, sends peacekeeping forces

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for quarrel is read backwards

parts.note: a row is a quarrel
thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: UN troops argue over an old military base of yours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks like a military camp, but it means low and contemptible.
explanation.definitionFit: Base means morally low, contemptible, lacking worth.

clue.text: Punch! Knockout … on my back!

indicators.note: back means the joined pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: KO is the abbreviation for a knockout in boxing
oh, as in oh my, is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A boxer is floored by a punch and ends up flat on his back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my!' is an exclamation of surprise, as is oh; 'back' turns the two joined pieces round together.
explanation.definitionFit: A hook is a short swinging punch in boxing.

clue.text: Also duke holds back honour

indicators.note: back means the hidden letters are read backwards
holds says the words Also duke contain the letters

explanation.surface: A duke also keeps his honour intact.
explanation.definitionFit: Kudos is praise and prestige won for an achievement.

clue.text: Tips trash can up on top of scrapheap

indicators.note: on top of in a down clue places the first piece above the second
in a down clue, up reads the word from the bottom

parts.note: a bin is a trash can

indicators.note: top of takes the opening letter of scrapheap

explanation.surface: A bin is tipped over on to a junk pile.
explanation.definitionFit: Nibs are the pointed tips of pens.

clue.text: The main way to greet a cyclist

parts.note: Sir Chris Hoy is a British Olympic track cycling champion

explanation.surface: The best way to say hello to someone on a bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' looks like principal but is the sea, as in the Spanish Main. Chris Hoy is a Scottish track cyclist with six Olympic golds.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahoy is the call sailors use to hail another ship.

clue.text: Standard place for hosting mostly a member of the nouveau-riche

parts.note: par is the standard, as in up to par

indicators.note: mostly removes the last letter of the word for place

parts.note: a venue is a place where something is held

explanation.surface: The usual spot for entertaining is now mostly hosting the newly wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for hosting' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu is an upstart who has newly risen to wealth but lacks breeding.

clue.text: Elected, Hillary's first meeting with Gore and Miliband did what Bill didn't

parts.note: a candidate who is elected is in

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of Hillary

parts.note: Al Gore was US vice-president
Ed Miliband was the UK Labour leader

explanation.surface: Politicians meet after an election, with a dig at Bill Clinton's famous denial.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill Clinton said he tried marijuana but did not inhale.
explanation.definitionFit: Clinton claimed he smoked cannabis without breathing it in, so the definition alludes to drawing smoke into the lungs.

clue.text: Treats mates for a buck and a quarter inside

indicators.note: inside places the compass point within the word for female deer

parts.note: a buck is a male deer, and does are female deer, its mates
S, south, is one quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone buys friends a drink for a dollar and a quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buck' and 'quarter' look like money; they are a male deer and a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Doses are measured amounts of medicine given to cure or treat.

clue.text: For example, Tess is rewritten without writers

indicators.note: without means outside, so the letters go around the other piece
rewritten means the letters are put down again in a new order

parts.note: say is used to introduce an example

explanation.surface: Tess's essay is redone without any authors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here: the anagram of TESS IS, signalled by 'rewritten', gives ESSIST, which goes around SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Essayists are authors of short prose pieces on a subject.
